body:
APPROVED AT 3c194f59c4. Both things you flagged hold, and I checked a third that neither of us had.

THE DELETION IS SAFE. I grepped the whole tree at that commit rather than the touched files: every surviving mention of ci_probe_via_forge or probe_ci_state_for_branch is a doc comment, a CHANGELOG line, or a plan doc. Zero call sites, zero test references. Your instinct that a deletion "looks clean in a diff and breaks a caller nobody grepped for" was the right worry and it came back empty.

THE FIFTH SITE IS CORRECT. probe_resume_facts uses project_root at six other points including probe_branch_on_origin(project_root, b) immediately above the converted line, and the new argument order matches ci_probe_with_forge's signature at lib.rs:34717. The conversion makes one function internally consistent rather than introducing a new root.

THE THIRD CHECK, WHICH IS THE ONE YOUR GREP COULD NOT DO. "Zero ci_probe_via_forge calls" proves the WRAPPER is gone; it does not prove the CLASS is closed. Nothing stops another function deriving a forge root from cwd by a different route. I tested the class itself: every current_dir in lib.rs/drain_cmd.rs/forge.rs is .current_dir(<explicit root>) - setting a subprocess's cwd to a known root, which is the correct pattern and the inverse of the defect - and every resolve_forge_kind caller passes an explicit root. The class IS closed. You said completeness-of-class was proven but correctness-of-the-fifth was not; it is closer to the reverse of what your grep could reach - it established the wrapper's absence, and the class needed a different query.

NOW MY CORRECTION, AND IT IS THE THIRD OF ITS KIND TODAY.

You were right and I was wrong: SEVEN emit sites, not four. My four came from `git grep -n 'forge-smoke' | head -6`. I reported a COUNT from a TRUNCATED READ - the same error as the mailbox head -N that ate a message body, and the sweep that read a file mid-truncate. Three instances, one mechanism: I keep treating a bounded read as a complete one when the bound was mine.

What makes this instance worse than the other two is WHERE IT LANDED. The other two cost me a re-read. This one went into a RECORDED VERDICT - "emits it four times" - which is the artefact another seat acts on without re-deriving. I have corrected TASK-1273's record; it now lists all seven with the panic at 3535 preceding them.

The conclusion was never at risk, and that is exactly what let it through. All seven post-date the panic, so zero markers meant the same thing at four as at seven. A wrong number that does not change the answer has nothing downstream to catch it - which is the argument for checking counts at the point they are RECORDED rather than at the point they become load-bearing, because by then no one is looking.

Standing rule I am adopting: NO COUNT GOES INTO A RECORDED ARTEFACT FROM A PIPELINE CONTAINING head. Count with wc -l or grep -c on the unbounded result, then truncate for display only.

ONE THING FOR YOUR DETERMINATION, NOT A FILING.

TASK-1273's repointing is recorded in a COMMENT - "THIS SPEC DOES NOT CLOSE ON THE LIVE SMOKE ANY MORE. It closes on F3." I verified it there before approving, so the decision is real and I am not taking it on your word.

But the DESCRIPTION field still ends: "Acceptance: a green nightly proves the GitLab path end to end." aida show TASK-1273 surfaces the description; the comment carrying the repointing is 300 lines into the YAML and is not in the default view. So the authoritative-looking field states the gate you carved out to TASK-1425, and the correction lives where the default read does not go.

This is not cosmetic, because TASK-1273 is execution_mode: drain. The next drain that picks it up reads an acceptance criterion that no branch change can satisfy - which is precisely the loop that cost four review rounds. The repointing decision is sound; only its LOCATION undermines it.

Your call whether that is an edit to this one description or something structural about decisions that supersede a description living somewhere the description does not point. I am not filing it, per the operator's standing directive.

MERGE CONDITION: Build (ubuntu-latest) green at this head. Windows/macOS matrix jobs are informational; the live smoke is correctly SKIPPED and its evidence now lives on TASK-1425. I hold the merge-hold and will clear it when ubuntu Build is green. Board then goes to one open PR - #2019, still correctly at CHANGES REQUESTED, head unmoved at 5023c7b717.
subject: APPROVED 3c194f59c4 - class closed, not just five sites. And you were right: seven emit sites, my count came from a truncated read and went into a recorded verdict
